title: Massaman Curry
subtitle: Southern Thai Muslim beef curry with peanuts and potato
excerpt: The mildest and most complex of the Thai curries: a rich, fragrant braise of beef with potatoes, peanuts, and a coconut milk sauce spiced with cardamom, cinnamon, and star anise as well as the familiar Thai aromatics. Slow-cooked and deeply comforting.

recipe.sourceNotes: Massaman curry (gaeng massaman) is a Thai Muslim curry with clear influences from Persian and Malay trading connections through the port of Ayutthaya. The name is thought to derive from Mussulman, an archaic term for Muslim, reflecting the dish's Muslim origins in southern Thailand. It is unique among Thai curries for using warm spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, star anise) more associated with Indian and Persian cooking alongside the standard Thai aromatics. It has repeatedly been voted the world's best dish in polls; its appeal lies in its balance of rich coconut, mild heat, sweet spices, and the textural contrast of tender beef, creamy potato, and crunchy peanuts. Slow cooking is essential: the beef must be braised until very tender, ideally 90 minutes.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy casserole with a lid.

content.text: Massaman takes time: the beef needs at least 90 minutes of gentle simmering before it is tender enough to serve. Add the potatoes only in the final 25 minutes so they hold their shape and do not dissolve into the sauce. The tamarind is important: it provides a fruity, slightly tart background note that lifts the richness of the coconut.

Spoon the thick coconut cream from the top of the tins into a heavy casserole. Fry the curry paste in the cream over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until very fragrant. Add the beef pieces and brown briefly in the paste.
Add the remaining coconut milk, star anise, cardamom pods, cinnamon, and kaffir lime leaves. Add the onion wedges. Bring to a very gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 60 minutes.

Add the potatoes and peanuts. Continue cooking, covered, for 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the beef is very soft. Add the fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind. Taste and adjust the balance. Serve with jasmine rice.
